entry.title: fix(output): keep a percent sign in a GitHub annotation (#1467)
entry.content:
fix(output): keep a percent sign in a GitHub annotation (#1467)

The github-actions reporter rewrote the message of every result, so a
policy message containing a percent sign reached the runner corrupted:

    $ conftest test -p policy.rego --output github svc.yaml
    ::error file=svc.yaml,line=1::replicas must be above 50%!o(MISSING)f node capacity

Percent signs are common in messages about ratios, and "%!o(MISSING)"
is not what the reviewer sees on the pull request.

writeLoc() applied fmt.Sprintf() to the message unconditionally, so
`msg` doubled as the format string of a call with no arguments and "%"
was read as a verb. The "(ORIGINATING FROM ...) " path in writeLocs()
then formatted the same message a second time.

A message is only a template when it arrives with arguments, so apply
Sprintf() in that case and resolve the message once, in writeLocs(),
before the location wrapper is added. The invariant that made
#1399 escape the file name -- a "%" already in the output line must
not be read as a verb by the final Fprintf -- is preserved, and now
also holds for the message itself.

The other reporters already pass the message as data (for instance
azuredevops.go uses Fprintf("... --> %s\n", ..., failure.Message)), so
github was the odd one out.

Signed-off-by: NUAAwqy <146524024+NUAAwqy@users.noreply.github.com>

entry.title: ci: add workflow to create release branches, document the rules (#1436)
entry.content:
ci: add workflow to create release branches, document the rules (#1436)

Add a workflow_dispatch workflow that creates releases/<version> from
master. It mints a token from a GitHub App scoped to an environment that
only trusts master, so the App can be the ruleset bypass actor instead
of every GITHUB_TOKEN, and it refuses to run for non-admins.

Document the matching rules: contributions target the v1 APIs on master
and need a separate PR against releases/0.x for the 0.x train, and v0.x
tags must be cut from releases/0.x since a tag on master would publish
v1 code as a v0 release.

Signed-off-by: James Alseth <james@jalseth.me>
